title: Finite-index transfer and horizontal homotopy on internal bar rows
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] on the small coherent profinite site in [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $G$ be a profinite group, meaning a compact Hausdorff totally disconnected topological group, and let $I^\bullet$ be a nonnegative cochain complex of internal $A$-modules with $A$-linear condensed $G$-action and equivariant differential [sk-def-sfb-module-objects, def-sfb-condensed-action-module, sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. No injectivity or resolution hypothesis on $I$ is imposed. For every open subgroup $J\subseteq G$, including $G$, form
$$D_J^{p,q}=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(A[\underline J^p],UI^q),\qquad p,q\geq0,$$
with the inhomogeneous action-dependent differential $d_h$ and commuting resolution differential $d_v$ of [def-sfb-condensed-equivariant-bar-data, def-sp-double-complex-total]. The symbol $U$ forgets the action, the free module is on the representable profinite parameter $J^p$, and internal Hom is right adjoint to internal module tensor. Let $r_H:D_G^{\bullet,\bullet}\to D_H^{\bullet,\bullet}$ be restriction along $H^p\hookrightarrow G^p$ for an open subgroup $H$ of $G$.
There are internal $A$-linear maps $t_H^{p,q}:D_H^{p,q}\to D_G^{p,q}$ and $h_H^{p,q}:D_G^{p,q}\to D_G^{p-1,q}$, zero for $p=0$, satisfying
$$d_ht_H=t_Hd_h,\qquad d_vt_H=t_Hd_v,\qquad d_vh_H=h_Hd_v,\qquad t_Hr_H-[G:H]1=d_hh_H+h_Hd_h.$$
They may be chosen, by fixing a finite coset transversal, naturally in equivariant chain maps of $I$. They commute with restriction along every map of profinite test sets. Thus for the internal vertical cohomology complexes $V_{J,q}^p=H^q(D_J^{p,\bullet},d_v)$, with kernels and sheaf images taken before section evaluation, they induce cochain maps $\bar t_H,\bar r_H$ and a horizontal homotopy. On the internal modules $E_J^{p,q}=H^p(V_{J,q}^\bullet,d_h)$ the induced maps satisfy
$$H^p(\bar t_H)H^p(\bar r_H)=[G:H]1_{E_G^{p,q}}.$$
The statement includes the zero ring, $H=G$, trivial $G$, and the zero complex. It asserts no vanishing and requires no rationality, norm topology, or completeness of coefficients.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-internal-bar-coefficient-transfer] to the fixed F,B,B_H. It supplies coefficient-natural restriction and transfer cochain maps and a coefficient-natural homotopy from their composite to multiplication by the subgroup index.

Apply the coefficient cochain functors and natural transformations termwise to a nonnegative equivariant complex, then flip the two complex directions as in [def-sfb-condensed-equivariant-bar-data, def-sp-double-complex-total]. In bidegree (p,q) the maps are the degree-p coefficient maps at I^q. Naturality in the coefficient differential makes these vertical chain maps. The horizontal homotopy has components at I^q; coefficient naturality makes each a vertical chain map as well. Its zero and boundary identities follow componentwise from the coefficient homotopy. Naturality for a chain map follows by applying coefficient naturality to each component. The evaluation of restriction is precisely the coefficient formula at I^q.

Apply the additive internal homology functor H^q to the horizontal homotopy of vertical complexes. Functoriality and additivity preserve composites, identities and the natural-number scalar, giving the required horizontal homotopy on vertical cohomology with components H^q(h_ij). Apply horizontal homology H^p: homotopic maps have equal homology maps (Mathlib Homotopy.homologyMap_eq), and homology preserves composites, identities and natural-number multiples. Thus H^p(r_bar) followed by H^p(t_bar) equals [G:H] times the identity. All homology is in the internal module category, before section evaluation.
